bull.b: Expansion of recurring revenue demonstrates that Growth Direct placements can generate continuing consumable and service demand after installation. Rising utilization and a larger validated base can improve revenue visibility and support compounding growth as more customers adopt routine automated testing workflows.

Consumables growth is a durable indicator of customer adoption because it reflects repeated use of the platform rather than only one-time instrument sales. Continued volume expansion can deepen customer integration, increase recurring revenue per installed system, and strengthen the platform’s long-term economics.

Improving gross and service margins show progress toward a more sustainable business model, particularly as service productivity and cost reductions take effect. Management’s targets for at least 20% gross margin in Q3 and mid-to-high 20s in Q4 indicate additional operating improvement may continue over the next several quarters.

bear.b: Large ongoing net and adjusted EBITDA losses indicate that revenue growth has not yet translated into operating leverage or self-funded expansion. Continued losses can consume capital, delay breakeven, and leave execution dependent on achieving future scale and margin improvements rather than current earnings power.

Persistent negative operating and free cash flow means the company is still consuming substantial cash while pursuing growth. Reliance on debt access and potential warrant proceeds increases financing and execution risk, and could constrain investment or dilute flexibility if internal cash generation does not improve.

A negative product margin means system sales currently do not cover their associated costs, limiting the profitability of the instrument-led growth engine. Although the trend is improving, sustained losses on products can offset recurring revenue gains until scale, pricing, software timing, or cost structure produces positive contribution.
